note: Textual function is not the same as canonicity, genre or truth. These are editorial classifications: 'provisional' means the catalogue has not consulted the relevant community formally; 'disputed' records a real disagreement rather than forcing one answer.

genesis.note: Canonical in Judaism and Christianity. 'Historical document' describes its ancient compositional setting, not the historicity of every narrative.

psalms.note: Canonical in Judaism and Christianity and used liturgically across many communities.

gospel-of-john.note: Canonical in Christianity. The historical-document classification refers to its function as an ancient biography, not to a claim of neutral historiography.

gospel-of-matthew.note: Canonical in Christianity. The historical-document classification refers to its function as an ancient biography, not to a claim of neutral historiography.

quran.note: Muslims confess the Qur’an as revealed scripture; recitation is central to worship. The classification records that claim and the text’s liturgical use.

bhagavad-gita.note: Bhagavad Gita — Scripture. Public-domain English translation streamed from Project Gutenberg.

dhammapada.note: Part of the Theravada Khuddaka Nikaya; its status and arrangement differ in other Buddhist canons. The complete Pali text and a CC0 translation are presented side by side.

guru-granth-sahib.note: Sikhs treat the Guru Granth Sahib as the living Guru, not merely as a book. The complete Gurmukhi and Khalsa English text is held locally under written permission from the Gurbani-CD rights holders.

tao-te-ching.note: Read as philosophy in some contexts and as a religious classic in others; its canonical status is not uniform.

analects.note: Analects — Classics. Complete public-domain English translation streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive (The Chinese Classics, vol. 1).

gathas.note: The Gathas are attributed to Zarathustra and are central to Zoroastrian liturgy.

acaranga-sutra.note: A Śvetāmbara Aṅga. The Digambara canon and its recensions differ, so the classification is not universal to all Jains.

kojiki.note: Kojiki — a court chronicle of myth and dynastic history. Shinto has no closed canon, so the chronicle is catalogued as a religiously authoritative historical document rather than as scripture.

apology.note: A literary defence speech set in Socrates' trial; its historicity and relationship to Plato's own views are debated.

meditations.note: Private Stoic notebooks rather than a public doctrinal text.

hidden-words.note: The Hidden Words — Scripture. The authorised English translation as the Bahá’í Reference Library publishes it, streamed from bahai.org (authoritative-texts/bahaullah/hidden-words).

kitab-i-aqdas.note: The Kitáb-i-Aqdas – The Most Holy Book — Scripture. The authorised English translation as the Bahá’í Reference Library publishes it, streamed from bahai.org (authoritative-texts/bahaullah/kitab-i-aqdas).

kitab-i-iqan.note: The Kitáb-i-Íqán – The Book of Certitude — Scripture. The authorised English translation as the Bahá’í Reference Library publishes it, streamed from bahai.org (authoritative-texts/bahaullah/kitab-i-iqan).

seven-valleys.note: The Seven Valleys — Scripture. The authorised English translation as the Bahá’í Reference Library publishes it, streamed from bahai.org (authoritative-texts/bahaullah/call-divine-beloved).

quaker-faith-and-practice.note: Britain Yearly Meeting's book of discipline. Other yearly meetings have their own books and may differ in theology and practice.

journal-of-george-fox.note: An autobiographical and historical account of the early Quaker movement, not a book of discipline.

uu-principles-and-sources.note: The 1985–2024 statement is historically situated; Unitarian Universalism has since adopted Shared Values language.

unitarian-christianity.note: A historical sermon, not a contemporary Unitarian Universalist statement.

ethical-movement.note: A movement address setting out Ethical Culture's principles and aims.

charge-of-the-goddess.note: A modern Wiccan liturgical text with multiple versions and attributions; it is not an ancient scripture.

book-of-mormon.note: Canonical for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Other Restorationist communities have different canons.

ofudesaki.note: A foundational Tenrikyo revelation. Official translations and permissions must be checked per edition.

phap-chanh-truyen.note: A foundational Cao Dai constitutional text. Different Cao Dai organisations may differ in authority and interpretation.

secret-doctrine.note: A modern Theosophical synthesis, not an ancient revealed text.

philosophy-of-freedom.note: A philosophical treatise by Rudolf Steiner, not an Anthroposophical scripture.

divine-principle.note: A foundational Unificationist text. Its status and authoritative edition are contested among Restorationist and Unificationist communities.

truth-of-life.note: A modern Seicho-no-Ie teaching text, not an ancient scripture.

reikai-monogatari.note: A modern Oomoto revelatory narrative. Its authority is specific to Oomoto and related communities.
